claims.text: RFC 6749 describes the access token as usually opaque to the client; it is meant for the resource server, and OAuth 2.0 itself defines no way for the client to learn who the user is.
claims.source_hint: RFC 6749 §1.4 Access Token ('usually opaque to the client'); OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §1 Introduction

claims.text: At stage-2 DonHang.App keeps only the access token from the token response (keycloak_sign_in.dart finish(): 'Only the access token is kept').
OpenID Connect is an identity layer on top of OAuth 2.0; a request is an OpenID Connect request when its scope contains openid, and the token response then contains an id_token next to access_token.
claims.source_hint: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §1, §3.1.2.1 (scope REQUIRED, MUST contain openid), §3.1.3.3 Successful Token Response

claims.text: The ID token is a JWT; its aud claim contains the client_id of the relying party (here donhang-app) and its sub claim is the issuer's identifier for the end user.
claims.source_hint: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §2 ID Token (iss, sub, aud); outputs/stage-2/scripts/backend/oidc-tokens.txt

claims.text: stage-2 output: scope 'profile email' gives no id_token, 'openid profile email' does; ID token aud donhang-app, access token aud donhang-api, same iss and sub. The access token also carries name and email; the script prints them only from the ID token.
In this realm donhang-app has profile and email as default client scopes, so the ID token carries the user's name and email even when only openid is requested.
claims.source_hint: keycloak/donhang-realm.json@stage-2:32 (defaultClientScopes); OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §5.4; Keycloak Server Admin Guide: Client scopes

claims.text: The realm's audience mapper on donhang-app adds donhang-api to aud of access tokens only (access.token.claim true, id.token.claim false).
JwtBearerOptions.Audience sets the single valid audience; with Audience = "donhang-api" a token whose aud is only donhang-app fails audience validation and the [Authorize] endpoint answers 401.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: configure JWT bearer authentication (Audience, ValidateAudience); DonHang.Api/Program.cs:48-50; oidc-tokens.txt (401 with ID token)

claims.text: The ID token and the access token of one sign-in are both JWTs signed by the same Keycloak realm (same iss), so in DonHang.Api the audience check is what separates them.
claims.source_hint: oidc-tokens.txt (same iss, different aud); Program.cs:40-56 (no other token-type check configured)

claims.text: The ID token is for the app to read; it is not meant to be sent to the API as an access token. At stage-2 DonHang.App keeps only the access token.
claims.source_hint: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §2 (ID Token audience is the client); RFC 6749 §7 (access token for protected resources)

claims.text: OpenID Connect runs on the same authorization code flow and token endpoint as OAuth 2.0; it is not a separate competing protocol.
claims.source_hint: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §1, §3.1 Authentication using the Authorization Code Flow

claims.text: jwt_claims in scripts/lib/keycloak.sh decodes the middle (payload) part of a JWT with jq.
